Deed Fraud: Protect Property in England and Wales

HM Land Registry's free Property Alert service covers England and Wales and warns about official searches or applications; it does not block them automatically.

By Alex Bacsa · Published 2026-06-15 · Updated 2026-07-10 · 3 min read

deed fraud UKproperty deed fraudproperty title fraudproperty ownership fraudprotect property deed
Key rule: verify through an official route you opened yourself, not the link, number, app, or payment details supplied by the suspicious message.

Being targeted right now? Do this

  1. Stop. Don’t pay, transfer money, or share passwords, PINs, or one-time codes.
  2. Contact your bank on the number on the back of your card if your money or details may be at risk.
  3. Report it — call Report Fraud on 0300 123 2040 (Police Scotland: 101), and forward scam texts to 7726.

Scope of this guide

The HM Land Registry services and forms below apply to England and Wales, not the whole UK. Scotland uses Registers of Scotland and Northern Ireland uses Land & Property Services. The original UK-wide title overstated the geographic scope of the detailed advice.

What property-title fraud looks like

A criminal uses a stolen or false identity to pose as an owner and attempts to sell or mortgage the property. HM Land Registry says risk is higher where identity has been stolen, the property is rented out, empty, owned by someone overseas, not mortgaged or not registered.

Warning signs

  • An unexpected Property Alert about an official search or application.
  • Correspondence about a sale, mortgage or register change that you did not authorise.
  • The contact address on the register is wrong or no longer monitored.

Property fraud remains relatively rare: HM Land Registry reported that 86 of more than 4.4 million applications in 2024–25 were identified as fraudulent. The risk is serious, but the article should not imply that title theft is common.

Property Alert

Property Alert is free and can monitor up to 10 registered properties in England and Wales. You do not have to own a property to monitor it. The service emails when HM Land Registry receives certain official searches or applications, but it does not automatically prevent a register change. Act promptly on an alert you do not recognise.

Title restrictions

An owner can apply for a restriction that prevents HM Land Registry registering a sale or mortgage unless a conveyancer or solicitor certifies that the application was made by the owner.

  • A private individual who does not live at the property can use Form RQ; there is no HM Land Registry fee.
  • An owner who lives at the property can apply using Form RX1; the current fee is £40.

A conveyancer may charge for providing a certificate when a later transaction takes place. The forms can be submitted by an owner, but legal advice may be useful where ownership or an existing application is disputed.

Protect the property

Register for Property Alert, keep the contact addresses on the register current, and consider a restriction if the risk factors apply. HM Land Registry permits up to three contact addresses, including an email address, but one must be postal.

If fraud may be happening

Contact the HM Land Registry Property Fraud Team at reportafraud@landregistry.gov.uk, or by phone using the number published on gov.uk's property-fraud guidance. HM Land Registry has processes for alteration or rectification of the register and a statutory indemnity scheme, but compensation depends on the legal conditions and the facts; it is not automatic in every fraud case.

Report the crime to Report Fraud in England or Wales at reportfraud.police.uk or 0300 123 2040. For a property in Scotland or Northern Ireland, use the relevant land-register and police routes for that jurisdiction.

Frequently asked questions

Does Property Alert stop a fraudulent sale?

No. It alerts you to certain activity so that you can investigate and act.

Is the non-resident-owner restriction completely free?

HM Land Registry charges no application fee for Form RQ, but a conveyancer may later charge to provide a required certificate.
